paraphrase: Dahui: nowadays some teachers of heretical silent-illumination Chan, seeing officials troubled by worldly affairs, teach them to become cold ashes and dead wood, a strip of white silk, an incense burner in an old shrine — but while the 'monkey' is not dead, how can there be rest? When he first went to Fujian he opposed this style strongly, calling it cutting off the life of buddha-wisdom.

location.section: Letters (書), juan 26: reply to Fu Shumi

paraphrase: Letter to Fu Shumi: press down at once the deluded mind, the discriminating mind, the mind that loves life and hates death, the mind of views and understanding, the mind that likes quiet and dislikes noise, and right there look at the critical phrase: 'does a dog have buddha-nature?' — 'wu'. This one word is a weapon that smashes all wrong knowledge. Do not understand it as being or non-being, nor by reasoning, nor by deliberation, nor in raising the eyebrows, nor in words, nor sink into the shell of no-concern, nor accept it where it is raised, nor seek proof in texts; only at all times, in all postures, keep raising it.

original.text: 但將妄想顛倒底心，思量分別底心，好生惡死底心，知見解會底心，欣靜厭鬧底心，一時按下，只就按下處看箇話頭
